title: Emrys and the Rivergate
premise: Ada Eriksen, estranged from their famous archaeologist mother and living rough along the Rivergate, discovers a tide-revealed cave holding relics that shouldn't exist—and evidence their mother vanished searching for the river's forbidden source. Pursued by the Rivergate Trust, a powerful consortium that has quietly owned the valley's secrets for generations, Ada follows the water upstream through drowned villages, hostile keepers, and their own buried grief. At the source, Ada learns the 'inheritance' their mother left is not treasure but proof of the Trust's founding crime, and that power over the valley was built on drowning the truth. In the end, Ada chooses to flood the archives—literally—releasing the source's waters and the records together, finding belonging not in legacy but in the community they once avoided.
about_author: Sable Blackwood is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping forgotten waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who belong to landscapes more than to families.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Ada Eriksen, living off-season in a shuttered boathouse, digs shell middens for cash and avoids the town that gossips about their mother. When an anomalous low tide exposes a cave mouth below the cliffs, Ada's professional instinct overrides caution. POV: Ada. Beat: restless isolation cracked open by curiosity.

chapters.title: Admission Charged by Legend
chapters.summary: Inside the cave, Ada finds carved toll-markers, a rusted lantern stamped with the Rivergate Trust crest, and fresh boot prints—someone else has been here recently. A near-fall into a tidal pool nearly traps them as the sea returns. POV: Ada. Beat: wonder shadowed by the first hint of danger.

chapters.title: What the Midden Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada catalogs finds at night: a child's shoe, a ledger page naming drowned villages, and a photograph of their mother, Dr. Ingrid Eriksen, dated three weeks ago. The realization lands: Ingrid came here and never left. POV: Ada. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Trust Sends Its Regards
chapters.summary: A courteous man named Aldous Vane visits the boathouse, offering money for 'any items recovered from the shoreline.' Ada lies smoothly and hates how easily lying comes. After he leaves, Ada finds the boathouse searched. POV: Ada. Beat: the invisible life ends; paranoia begins.

chapters.title: Upstream Is a Direction, Not a Plan
chapters.summary: Ada decides to follow the Rivergate to its source, where Ingrid's notes point. They barter supplies from ferry-woman Bryn Halvard, who asks no questions but watches too carefully. First day on the river: beautiful, deceptively easy. POV: Ada. Beat: commitment—the point of no return crossed lightly.

chapters.title: Drowned Steeple, Rising Fog
chapters.summary: Ada passes the flooded ruins of Old Merrow, a village the maps say never existed. Underwater bells chime without wind. Bryn catches up by boat and admits her grandmother was born there. POV: Ada, then a brief Bryn interlude. Beat: the past is physically present; alliance forms.

chapters.title: Keepers of the Weir
chapters.summary: At a stone weir, uniformed Trust wardens turn travelers back with polite menace. Ada slips past at night using digger's techniques to read the terrain, but loses their pack and half their food. POV: Ada. Beat: competence tested; cost made real.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Second Page
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a hollow tree, Ada studies the ledger fragment: payments made annually since 1893 to families who 'accepted relocation.' The Trust didn't just own the valley—it emptied it. POV: Ada. Beat: theme crystallizes—inheritance as complicity.

chapters.title: Bryn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bryn reveals she's been paid by the Trust for years to report strangers on the river; she never reported Ada. She offers to carry Ada to Gallowford if Ada lets her see the ledger. POV: Bryn. Beat: trust extended despite betrayal; moral complexity deepens.

chapters.title: Gallowford's Polite Hunger
chapters.summary: The mill-town of Gallowford thrives on Trust patronage. Ada poses as a surveyor, gathering rumors: Ingrid passed through weeks ago asking about the 'Headwaters House.' Vane's agents are asking the same questions behind her. POV: Ada. Beat: cat-and-mouse tightens.

chapters.title: A Room With Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: In Gallowford's inn, Ada finds Ingrid stayed in room four and left pencil marks inside the wardrobe—a map fragment and one word: 'Ask the bell-keeper.' Ada sleeps in their mother's bed and weeps for the first time in years. POV: Ada. Beat: intimacy with the lost parent; resolve hardened by sorrow.

chapters.title: The Bell-Keeper's Toll
chapters.summary: The old bell-keeper of Gallowford, half-blind Marta, demands a story as payment. Ada tells the truth about their mother for the first time aloud. Marta answers with a route through the fens and a warning: 'The source doesn't want to be found. It wants to be understood.' POV: Ada. Beat: confession as passage; wisdom received.

chapters.title: Fen Water Rising
chapters.summary: The fen crossing goes wrong when Trust dredges, disguised as maintenance, raise the water level deliberately. Ada and Bryn are separated. Ada survives by climbing into a drowned church tower as night falls. POV: Ada. Beat: isolation again, but now chosen company is missed.

chapters.title: Vane's Version of History
chapters.summary: Vane finds Ada stranded—not by accident, he admits—and offers a ride and a narrative: the Trust prevents floods, funds towns, keeps order. 'Your mother wanted chaos dressed as truth.' He leaves food and a choice. POV: Ada. Beat: temptation articulated well enough to shake.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Ferry Ruin
chapters.summary: Ada and Bryn reunite; Bryn confesses she took Trust money again—for fuel, nothing more. Their argument cracks into honesty about debt, survival, and what clean hands cost. They go on together, terms explicit. POV: alternating. Beat: relationship rebuilt on truth instead of convenience.

chapters.title: The Salmon Ladder
chapters.summary: Following fish upstream past impossible rapids, Ada reads the landscape like a stratigraphy: every 'natural' barrier is engineered. The river itself has been managed for a century. Someone controls the water. POV: Ada. Beat: scale of the conspiracy revealed through craft.

chapters.title: Headwaters House
chapters.summary: They reach a manor built directly over the river's emergence, elegant and wrong, its gardens irrigated while downstream villages flood. Wardens patrol. From a ridge, Ada sees lights in a lower gallery—and a figure moving. POV: Ada. Beat: arrival at the threshold; dread and hope entwined.

chapters.title: In Through the Culvert
chapters.summary: Using an eighteenth-century drainage culvert from Ingrid's map fragment, Ada enters the house's underbelly. Bryn stays outside as lookout. Inside: humming machinery, cold air, and walls lined with sealed archive doors. POV: Ada. Beat: infiltration; claustrophobic tension.

chapters.title: The Archive of Drowned Things
chapters.summary: Ada finds rooms of salvaged village records, personal effects, and photographs—everything taken from relocated families, catalogued like specimens. Including the Eriksen family Bible. Their name is in it. POV: Ada. Beat: personal stake detonates inside the political one.

chapters.title: A Voice From the Gallery
chapters.summary: Following the figure, Ada finds Ingrid alive—imprisoned by circumstance, not bars: she's been translating the Trust's founding documents under duress, trading cooperation for access. Reunion is not warm. Ingrid says: 'You shouldn't have come.' POV: Ada. Beat: reunion complicated by resentment; love and anger coexisting.

chapters.title: The Founding Crime
chapters.summary: Ingrid shows Ada the original 1893 charter: the Trust's founders dynamited a natural spring system to control flow, drowning five villages and rewriting maps. Every flood since was policy. The source isn't forbidden—it's evidence. POV: Ingrid flashback interwoven with present. Beat: full revelation; theme of corrupted power made concrete.

chapters.title: Why She Left
chapters.summary: Ingrid explains her years of absence: she discovered the family were charter signatories and couldn't face Ada carrying that inheritance. Ada's fury finally breaks—then settles into something harder than forgiveness: partnership. POV: Ada. Beat: emotional climax of the family arc.

chapters.title: Vane Closes the Trap
chapters.summary: Vane, aware of the breach, seals the culvert and offers final terms: the Eriksens join the Trust publicly, legitimizing it, or disappear like the villages did. He genuinely believes order justifies everything. POV: Ada. Beat: antagonist at full strength; stakes existential.

chapters.title: Bryn Rings the Bell
chapters.summary: Outside, Bryn commandeers Gallowford's church bell and rings the old alarm pattern her grandmother taught her—the signal of the drowned villages. Downstream, lights come on in windows. People remember. POV: Bryn. Beat: the silenced find voice; hope mobilizes.

chapters.title: The Keepers Waver
chapters.summary: Wardens, many local, hear the bell and hesitate. One unlocks a corridor and walks away. Power, Ada realizes, runs on consent, and consent is leaking. POV: Ada. Beat: the machine develops cracks from within.

chapters.title: Flood the Archives
chapters.summary: Ada proposes the unthinkable: breach the reservoir gates and let the source reclaim Headwaters House, destroying the archive—but the water will also reach downstream unless the old sluices, which only the bell-keepers know, are opened in sequence. POV: Ada. Beat: plan formed; terrible trade-off accepted.

chapters.title: Marta's Sequence
chapters.summary: Marta, brought upriver by Bryn's message, recites the sluice order from a song every drowned-village child once learned. 'They took our land,' she says, 'but not the tune.' POV: Marta. Beat: inherited culture becomes the instrument of justice—inheritance redeemed.

chapters.title: Opening the First Gate
chapters.summary: Ada and Ingrid descend into the spring chamber together, mother and child doing fieldwork side by side for the first time. They hand-crank the ancient gate against resistance as water groans behind it. POV: Ada. Beat: reconciliation enacted through shared labor.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Vane confronts them at the second gate, alone, gun drawn, making his truest case: without the Trust, the valley floods and someone must be blamed. Ingrid answers: 'Then let it be weather, not owners.' Ada trips the gate. POV: Ada. Beat: ideological climax; the antagonist defeated by refusal, not force.

chapters.title: The Source Unbound
chapters.summary: Water takes the house floor by floor. Ada, Ingrid, and Marta climb toward the roof as archives drown below—ledgers, charters, the machinery of memory-control dissolving. Ada feels grief and liberation at once. POV: Ada. Beat: climax peak; destruction as release.

chapters.title: Roofline Rescue
chapters.summary: Bryn navigates her ferry through the surge to the roof. Vane, refusing rescue, remains with his house. The four escape downriver on a flood they helped choose, steering by Marta's song. POV: Bryn. Beat: escape earned; loss acknowledged without regret.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Days later, the valley assesses itself: fields silted, roads gone, but the river running clear and free for the first time in a century. Villages begin returning to higher ground their grandparents named in songs. POV: Ada. Beat: aftermath honest about cost; renewal visible.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: The flood deposits artifacts on new banks—relocated families' belongings returned by the current. People come to claim them. Ada, digging again, helps match objects to descendants. POV: Ada. Beat: archaeology repurposed from extraction to restitution.

chapters.title: The Trust Without Vane
chapters.summary: Remnant Trust members, led by a warden who unlocked the corridor, propose a new charter: water managed openly, records public, descendants seated at the table. Ada is asked to sign. POV: Ada. Beat: power offered back; the corruption test repeated.

chapters.title: Signing and Refusing
chapters.summary: Ada signs as a witness, not an owner—refusing inheritance of control while accepting responsibility. Ingrid does the same. 'Belonging isn't a deed,' Ada writes in the margin. POV: Ada. Beat: thematic resolution; the lesson stated through action.

chapters.title: Room Four, Revisited
chapters.summary: Ada and Ingrid return to Gallowford's inn. In the wardrobe, Ingrid adds new pencil marks beside her old ones: a map of the free river, and both their names. They laugh for the first time together in the book. POV: Ada. Beat: tenderness after rupture; quiet joy.

chapters.title: The Cave at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ada revisits the original cave. The tide no longer reveals it—or Ada no longer needs it to. They leave the ledger's last page there, face-up, for whoever the sea chooses next. POV: Ada. Beat: circular closure; mystery honored rather than solved.

chapters.title: Bryn's Route
chapters.summary: Bryn launches a ferry service along the restored river, telling passengers the true history as she poles them upstream. Her grandmother's village gets a marker stone. POV: Bryn. Beat: secondary arc resolved; storytelling as keeping-alive.

chapters.title: Field Notes for a Stranger
chapters.summary: Ada begins writing a book—not of treasure, but of water, songs, and the people who kept both. The last entry describes teaching a child to read a riverbank. POV: Ada. Beat: identity transformed from invisible to witness.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years on, the river bears its old name again—Emrys, from a song Marta sang. Ada stands at the source, now a spring-fed pool ringed by wildflowers, and lets the silence hold. Some inheritances you refuse; some you become. POV: Ada. Beat: peace earned; the title's meaning fulfilled.
